gym.intro: Best gym defenders: the ones that last longest and still hit back. No legendary, mythical, Ultra Beast, Shadow or Mega Pokémon.
gym.method1: A defender mostly lasts: it costs attackers time and potions. So bulk weighs most, its defender HP (doubled in a gym) times its defense, and its damage a bit less: bulk^1.5 × DPS^0.5, at level 40 with 15/15/15 IVs, with its best moveset against a neutral target.
gym.method2: Bulk is its score against the first one, which is 100. Legendary, mythical, Ultra Beast, Shadow and Mega Pokémon cannot defend gyms; filtering by type does not change the rank.

top.weatherLegendHelp: In amber, the number with the weather that boosts its charged move type: its moves deal 20% more
top.methodWeather: In amber, below, the same with the weather that boosts its charged move type (Sunny for Fire, Rain for Water…): moves of that weather's types deal 20% more. The order does not change; it shows how much it would gain.
top.edpsHelp: The closest to a real raid: damage per second minus the time you lose each time it faints. The one that tells you who to power up.
top.dpsHelp: What it deals while it stays up, ignoring the time you lose when it faints.
top.tdoHelp: Rewards the ones that stay alive and keep hitting.
top.pveIntro: Best raid attackers, type by type. Under “All”, the ones with the best average against every boss.
top.pvpIntro: PvPoke ranking with the recommended moveset.
top.method1: Level 40 with 15/15/15 IVs against the bosses weak to the list's type: the legendary, Ultra Beast, Mega and mythical Pokémon that have been raid bosses, with 180 defense. Each boss hits you according to its moves: if they are super effective against your Pokémon, it faints sooner. Each Pokémon uses its best moveset against them, which must include a move of that type (the other may be of another type: Black Kyurem appears in Dragon with Freeze Shock, which also hits them for ×1.6 or more), and each move deals to each boss what it would in the game; the figure is the average. Normal has no weak bosses, so it uses a neutral one with a Normal charged move. For a specific boss, check its counters on the raids page.
top.methodTier: The letter comes from the rank, with the cutoffs of GO Hub's overall list: S up to 20, A+ up to 50, A up to 100, B+ up to 150, B up to 200, C up to 250, D up to 300 and F beyond. In a single type's list the cutoffs are a fifth: S up to 4, A+ up to 10, A up to 20…
top.methodAll: “All” ranks by the average eDPS against every raid boss, each Pokémon with a single moveset: the one with the best average. It rewards Pokémon that work against many bosses, not those that shine in one or two types.
top.method2: Sorted by eDPS, the damage per second it really adds in a raid. Each life starts with no energy, as in the game: fast moves until the bar fills (incoming damage charges it too), and only charged moves that land before it faints count. The boss deals 1333 divided by your defense per second, like a tier 5 boss; that sets how long it lasts and its TDO. eDPS takes off 2.3 s each time it faints (the next one coming in, and rejoining every six): that is why a glass cannon drops even if it hits hard. Super Mega «+» moves deal ×1.3, their power at Mega Level 4 (Super Max). It does not model dodging.
top.method3: Frustration and Return are excluded: they are not real options for an optimized attacker.
top.legacyHelp: Turn it off to see only movesets you can still get: some Pokémon rank high thanks to a move that is no longer learnable.
top.eliteHelp: Turn it off to see only movesets you can get with regular TMs: Elite moves need an Elite TM or a specific event.
top.legendaryHelp: Legendary and Mythical Pokémon: only in five-star Max Battles on set dates.

max.title: Max Battles
max.intro: Fought at Power Spots against Dynamax and Gigantamax Pokémon.
max.upgradeNote: Total across all three levels, unlock included.
max.tabIntro: The Max Move takes the type of the fast attack. By damage: power × attack × STAB.
max.noneOfType: No Dynamax of this type yet.
max.battlesNote: Announced Max Battles show up here. Which Pokémon each Power Spot currently hosts is not published anywhere: it rotates by area and is only visible in-game.
max.liveSource: The higher CP is a 100 % IV catch. Data from Snacknap, which publishes the Power Spot roster.
max.teamIntro: Against {pokemon}: one to tank with Max Guard and two hitting with their Max Move.
max.teamAgainst: To beat {pokemon} in a Max Battle
max.noAttackers: No Dynamax has a type advantage here.
max.teamNote: Ranked by attack, STAB and type advantage, not by damage: Max Moves have no published power. The Max Move takes the type of the fast attack, so each one gets its best. Evolving keeps the Dynamax form.
max.globalPool: Each Power Spot picks a random boss from this list and rotates.
max.stabHelp: If the move matches one of the Pokémon’s types, it deals 20% more damage (×1.2).
max.stabTitle: Same type as the Pokémon: 20% more damage
max.calcLegend: Calculated with the Max Move at level 3 (the maximum) and every Pokémon at the same level with 15/15/15 IVs.
max.method1: A Dynamax Pokémon’s Max Move takes the type of its fast attack; a Gigantamax Pokémon uses its own fixed G-Max Move.
max.method2: Ranked by the damage of that move, with the game formula: power × attack × STAB. G-Max Moves and the exclusive ones (Crowned Zacian and Zamazenta, Eternatus) have 450 power; Max Moves, 350.
max.gmaxBorderLegend: Fuchsia border: Gigantamax, with its own move

rolesLegend.atacante: Attacker: its rank in this list, by damage
rolesLegend.tanque: Tank: holds on with Max Guard (defense × HP)

max.methodRoles: The three letters on each row: as an attacker, from its rank in this list; as a tank, by defense × HP, how long it lasts using Max Guard; and as a healer, by its HP, since Max Spirit heals based on HP. Tank and healer are ranked among every Pokémon that can Dynamax. The game does not publish how much Max Guard blocks or Max Spirit heals: this is a ranking, not a prediction.
